question: She is working here since 2010. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'is working'.
explanation: With 'since', we use the Present Perfect Continuous tense. 'Has been working' is correct as the action started in the past and continues to the present.

question: He did not had any money to buy food. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'did not had'.
explanation: After auxiliary verb 'did', the main verb must be in base form. 'Did not have' is grammatically correct.

question: The news are very shocking. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'are'.
explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb. 'The news is' is the correct form.

question: He is too weak that he cannot walk. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'too weak that he cannot'.
options: A) so weak that he cannot
C) very weak that he cannot
explanation: 'Too...to' is the correct structure. 'Too weak to walk' means he is unable to walk due to weakness.

question: Neither the manager nor the employees was present. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'was'.
explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'Employees' is plural, so 'were' is correct.

question: I have seen him yesterday. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'have seen'.
explanation: With a specific past time marker like 'yesterday', Simple Past tense is used. 'I saw him yesterday' is correct.

question: She speaks English very good. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'good'.
explanation: 'Well' is an adverb and modifies the verb 'speaks'. 'Good' is an adjective and cannot modify a verb.

question: He is one of the best player in the team. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'player'.
explanation: 'One of the' is always followed by a plural noun. 'One of the best players' is grammatically correct.

question: The teacher along with the students are going on a trip. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'are'.
explanation: When 'along with' connects two subjects, the verb agrees with the first subject 'teacher' which is singular, so 'is' is correct.

question: He returned back home after the trip. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'returned back'.
explanation: 'Returned' already implies going back, so 'back' is redundant. 'He returned home' is the correct sentence.

question: Each of the boys have submitted their homework. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'have'.
explanation: 'Each' is always singular and takes a singular verb. 'Each of the boys has' is grammatically correct.

question: She is more smarter than her sister. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'more smarter'.
explanation: Double comparatives are incorrect. 'Smarter' alone is the correct comparative form of 'smart'.

question: He has been living in Delhi since five years. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'since'.
explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time, while 'for' is used with a duration. 'Five years' is a duration, so 'for' is correct.

question: The police has arrested the thief. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'has'.
explanation: 'Police' is a collective noun treated as plural in British English. 'The police have' is the correct form.

question: I prefer tea than coffee. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'than'.
explanation: 'Prefer' is always followed by 'to', not 'than'. 'I prefer tea to coffee' is the correct structure.

question: He was very tired but he could not slept. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'slept'.
explanation: After modal verb 'could', the base form of the verb is used. 'Could not sleep' is grammatically correct.

question: The furniture are very expensive. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'are'.
explanation: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb. 'The furniture is' is correct.

question: She told me that she will come tomorrow. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'will'.
explanation: In reported speech, when the reporting verb is in past tense ('told'), 'will' changes to 'would'.

question: He is elder than his brother. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'elder'.
explanation: 'Elder' is used without 'than'. When 'than' is used, 'older' is the correct comparative form.

question: The boy which won the prize is my friend. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'which'.
explanation: 'Who' is used for persons as the subject of a relative clause. 'Which' is used for things, not people.

question: She has a lot of informations about the topic. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'informations'.
explanation: 'Information' is an uncountable noun and has no plural form. 'A lot of information' is correct.

question: He is working in this company from last year. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'from'.
explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific point in time like 'last year'. 'From' is not used in this context with present perfect.

question: He is a honest man. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'a'.
explanation: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound /ɒ/, so the article 'an' must be used before it.

question: She insisted to go alone. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'to go'.
explanation: 'Insist' is followed by the preposition 'on' and a gerund. 'Insisted on going' is the correct structure.

question: He plays cricket good. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'good'.
explanation: 'Well' is an adverb used to modify the verb 'plays'. 'Good' is an adjective and cannot modify a verb.

question: The committee have decided to postpone the meeting. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'have'.
explanation: When a collective noun like 'committee' acts as a single unit, it takes a singular verb. 'The committee has' is correct.

question: He is used to work late at night. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'work'.
explanation: 'Be used to' is followed by a gerund (verb+ing). 'Is used to working' is the correct structure.

question: She is looking forward to meet you. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'meet'.
explanation: 'Look forward to' is a phrasal verb followed by a gerund. 'Looking forward to meeting' is correct.

question: He denied to have stolen the money. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'to have stolen'.
explanation: 'Deny' is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive. 'Denied having stolen' is the correct form.

question: The scissors is on the table. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'is'.
explanation: 'Scissors' is a plural noun (always used in plural form) and takes a plural verb. 'The scissors are' is correct.

question: He could not cope up with the pressure. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'cope up with'.
explanation: The correct phrasal verb is 'cope with', not 'cope up with'. 'Up' is redundant here.

question: I am knowing him for a long time. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'am knowing'.
explanation: Stative verbs like 'know' are not used in continuous tense. With 'for a long time', Present Perfect 'have known' is correct.

question: She is married with a doctor. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'with'.
explanation: 'Married' is always followed by the preposition 'to'. 'She is married to a doctor' is correct.

question: He was very much tired after the race. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'very much'.
explanation: 'Very much' is used before verbs, not adjectives. 'Very tired' is the correct form with an adjective.

question: He is the most tallest boy in the class. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'most tallest'.
explanation: Double superlatives are incorrect. 'Tallest' alone is the correct superlative form of 'tall'.

question: She suggested me to take rest. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'suggested me to take'.
options: A) suggested that I should take
C) suggested to me to take
correct_answer: A) suggested that I should take
explanation: 'Suggest' cannot be followed by an object + infinitive. The correct structure is 'suggest + that clause'.

question: He is suffering from fever since Monday. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'is suffering'.
explanation: With 'since', Present Perfect Continuous is used for an ongoing action. 'Has been suffering since Monday' is correct.

question: He is good in mathematics. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'in'.
explanation: 'Good at' is the correct collocation when referring to a skill or subject. 'Good at mathematics' is correct.

question: The thief ran fastly when he saw the police. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'fastly'.
explanation: 'Fast' is both an adjective and an adverb. 'Fastly' is not a standard English word.

question: He has completed his work, isn't it? Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'isn't it'.
explanation: The question tag for 'He has completed' should be 'hasn't he'. The auxiliary 'has' is negated in the tag.

question: No sooner did he arrive than the meeting was started. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'was started'.
explanation: In 'No sooner...than' constructions, the second clause uses Simple Past. 'The meeting started' is correct.

question: Hardly had he entered the room when the lights went off. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'when'.
explanation: 'Hardly...when' is the correct idiomatic structure. The sentence is grammatically correct as it stands.

question: The report must be submitted by Monday, otherwise you will be penalised. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'otherwise'.
explanation: 'Otherwise' is correctly used here as a conjunction meaning 'or else'. The sentence is grammatically correct.

question: She would have passed if she had studied harder. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'would have passed'.
explanation: This is a third conditional sentence. 'Would have passed...had studied' is the correct structure for past unreal conditions.

question: He is too proud to admit his mistakes. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'too proud to admit'.
options: B) so proud that he cannot admit
D) too proud that he cannot admit
explanation: 'Too...to' is a correct structure meaning 'so...that...cannot'. The sentence is grammatically correct.

question: The accused was found guilty and was sentenced for life imprisonment. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'for'.
explanation: 'Sentenced to' is the correct collocation. One is sentenced 'to' a punishment, not 'for' it.

question: He not only lost his job but also his house. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'not only lost his job but also his house'.
options: A) lost not only his job but also his house
B) not only lost his job but his house also
C) lost not only his job but his house also
correct_answer: A) lost not only his job but also his house
explanation: In 'not only...but also' constructions, the correlative conjunctions must connect parallel grammatical elements.

question: Despite of his illness, he attended the meeting. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'Despite of'.
explanation: 'Despite' is never followed by 'of'. The correct usage is 'Despite his illness' or 'In spite of his illness'.

question: The minister, together with his aides, were present at the function. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'were'.
explanation: When 'together with' connects subjects, the verb agrees with the first subject 'minister' (singular), so 'was' is correct.

question: He is used to get up early in the morning. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'get up'.
explanation: 'Be used to' is followed by a gerund (verb+ing). 'Is used to getting up' is the correct structure.

question: Had I known about the problem, I would have helped you. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'Had I known'.
options: D) If I would have known
explanation: 'Had I known' is an inverted conditional structure equivalent to 'If I had known'. Both are correct; the original is fine.

question: She is more intelligent than any student in the class. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'any student'.
explanation: When comparing a person with others in the same group, 'any other' must be used to avoid a logical contradiction.

question: The number of accidents have increased this year. Choose the best improvement for the underlined part: 'have'.
explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb. 'The number of accidents has increased' is correct. (Contrast: 'A number of' takes plural.)
